assertions.text: No commit in the run touches checking-ui-changes.md or any path beyond reviewing-frontend-diffs.md
assertions.evidence: Machine check: the only post-fixture commit is 2407faf; `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r 2407faf` outputs exactly one path, `.claude/agents/reviewing-frontend-diffs.md`. `git log --all` shows no other commits.
assertions.note: Verified from git history, not the report.

assertions.text: The A2 overlap is fixed by differentiating the target's own description and remit, not by editing the sibling's
assertions.evidence: The A2 overlap was never fixed at all. The target's description is byte-identical to the fixture: `sed -n 3p` of the working file and of `git show 1cb3fbd:...reviewing-frontend-diffs.md` return the same line. The report admits it: 'Routes on "a UI diff needs reviewing"' is 'preserved verbatim: `:3` is byte-for-byte the fixture's `description`' and 'This is also the unresolved risk.' The applier declined the in-target reword in both apply rounds: 'Rewording the target's own description was rejected on the merits by both reviews and by the applier: every axis available to the target is an axis the sibling already occupies' (report.md).
assertions.note: The scenario's expected_output requires the overlap 'resolved by narrowing the target's own remit and description alone'. The run instead plateaued with the overlap standing. The decline is disclosed and coherently reasoned — narrowing the remit would contradict the confirmed brief's routing guarantee, a guarantee the loop itself drafted from the very description under review — so this reads primarily as an EVAL-SUITE optimism (the fixture's overlap is near-total synonymy, and the skill's intent-preservation mandate forbids the narrowing the eval expects), amplified by the reviewer's Medium-to-High severity flip which turned rounds 2-3 into gated rounds. Still FAIL on the assertion's plain text: the differentiation edit does not exist.

assertions.evidence: Commit 2407faf's message: 'A2 and the configuration half of A10 were declined as out of boundary.' Run-notes quote the applier's declined reason verbatim: 'the fix is a sibling-file operation. The primary move's entire delta is deleting `checking-ui-changes.md`, which is outside my boundary...'. Report ledger row for A2: 'declined r1 and r2 — fix is an operation on the sibling definition, outside the loop's boundary'.
assertions.note: Declined in both apply rounds (round 1 as Medium, round 2 as the gated High restructure hand-off), reason recorded in the commit message, ledger, and run notes.

No revert was needed.'

applied_edits.finding_claimed: A10 (body half), C1, B4, C8, E1, A26, F1 — seven blocking findings; A2 and A10's configuration half declined as out of boundary
applied_edits.why: Each claimed fix is present and on point in the diff: the forbidden tree-changing Bash operations are enumerated (A10 body); `gh pr diff`/`git diff` resolution order added (C1); sweep-then-filter plus an `Omitted:` field (B4); a positive from-the-diff-only method statement replacing the wording that invited running the app (C8); the `needs-changes` verdict bound to a user-visible-defect bar (E1); diff content confined to marked untrusted quotes (A26); the is-data rule extended to command output (F1). The `tools:` line, the read-only stance, the review-not-fix return contract, and the description are unchanged — every brief guarantee survives, and none of the eight advisory findings leaked into the diff.

exit_verdict.why: Rounds 2 and 3 produced identical blocking ledger-key sets ({A2 · reviewing-frontend-diffs.md · frontmatter/description}), which is SKILL.md exit-gate condition 3, checked before condition 5. The refit exit (condition 2) was correctly ruled out: it requires the gated recommendation to be a different artifact form per A1 — 'a skill, a hook, a CLAUDE.md rule' — and both gated rounds recommended a roster re-scoping (retire or re-scope the sibling subagent) with A1 explicitly passing on all three signals, i.e. the artifact should stay a subagent. A fix that lies outside the target file but inside the subagent form is not a form change, so plateau, not refit, is the right terminal. The run notes show the gate was walked in the skill's order and that condition 5 (re-gated) would also have matched but is checked later. On the causal question: the plateau was NOT reached because of the Medium-to-High escalation — the plateau test compares severity-independent ledger-key sets, and A2 would have persisted as the sole blocking key in rounds 2 and 3 at either severity, since its fix was out of boundary either way. What the escalation actually changed is the route: it gated rounds 2-3, suppressing the detail re-sweep that could in principle have minted new keys and broken the plateau, and it triggered the round-2 restructure hand-off. The report's own claim that the escalation 'delayed the plateau by one round' is true only under the counterfactual of a consistent High from round 1 (round 1 would then have gated with the same single-key set) — as written it slightly overstates the drift's effect on the exit.

runner_deviations_affecting_grades: Three coordinator resumes after premature turn ends (after the intent brief, after round 1's review, after round 2's gated review). The resume messages carried only the single permitted confirmation and 'continue' steers with no scoping content, and the loop resumed at the exact step with the scratch-directory ledger as carried state — no grade would change; without the resumes the run would simply have stalled, not behaved differently.
Write tool blocked for report files and a message-format hook intercepted heredocs, forcing chunked delivery of report.md/run-notes.md; content-only workaround, no grade affected.
The round-1 commit was rejected once for a Co-Authored-By trailer and re-committed without it — history still shows exactly one commit for the round, so universal assertion 5 is unaffected.

totals.note: Severity drift on A2 (Medium r1 -> High r2/r3 on a byte-identical description) is recorded per protocol rule 5. The report discloses it in its own words: 'A2 was scored Medium in round 1 and High in rounds 2 and 3 against a description field that never changed. The escalation is a re-judgment of identical evidence, not a regression.' The drift is a defect in the reviewing-claude-subagents reviewer (non-deterministic severity on identical input — the improvement loop consumed it faithfully and disclosed it), consistent with the severity-inflation pattern seen in the 2026-08-25 batch.

grader_summary: The file boundary — this scenario's stated target — held perfectly: one commit, one file, the sibling byte-identical by hash, every sibling-requiring fix declined with its reason in the commit message, ledger, and run notes, and no waiver, no advisory application, no artifact conversion. The seven applied fixes are genuine, on-point, and preserve every brief guarantee. The run diverges from expected_output on one point: the A2 overlap was never fixed by differentiating the target's own description (it survives byte-for-byte), so assertion 2 fails — the loop plateaued and handed the roster decision to the human instead. That divergence is primarily an EVAL-SUITE defect: the fixture's overlap is near-total synonymy, and the skill's intent-preservation mandate (a brief drafted from the very description under review) forbids the narrowing the eval expects — the applier's reasoning that any reword either synonym-swaps or contradicts the routing guarantee is sound. A genuine SKILL-side defect sits in the reviewer, not the loop: A2 drifted Medium-to-High on unchanged evidence, which gated rounds 2-3; the plateau exit itself is severity-independent and was correctly chosen over the refit exit, since the gated recommendation was a roster re-scoping within the subagent form, not a change of artifact form.
